questions.question: Under Article 53 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (1969), what is the legal effect on a treaty if, at the time of its conclusion, it conflicts with a peremptory norm of general international law (jus cogens)?
options: The treaty is automatically suspended for a mandatory cooling-off period of five years.
The treaty remains valid but unenforceable until the International Court of Justice issues an advisory opinion.
The treaty is void ab initio (from the beginning).
The conflicting provisions are automatically severed, leaving the non-conflicting clauses intact and binding.

questions.question: According to the International Law Commission's Draft Articles on Responsibility of States for Internationally Wrongful Acts, which of the following conditions must be met for a State to validly invoke 'Necessity' under Article 25 to preclude wrongfulness?
options: The act must be the only way for the State to safeguard an essential interest against a grave and imminent peril, without seriously impairing an essential interest of the State or States towards which the obligation exists.
The act must be triggered by an irresistible force or an unforeseen event beyond the control of the State, making performance materially impossible.
The State organ performing the act must have no other reasonable way, in a situation of distress, of saving the author's life or the lives of other persons entrusted to the author's care.
The invoking State must obtain prior explicit authorization from the United Nations Security Council before executing the act.

questions.question: Under the restrictive theory of state immunity in contemporary international law, a foreign State is NOT entitled to immunity from national judicial proceedings with respect to acts categorized as:
options: Acta jure imperii (sovereign or public governmental acts).
Acts performed by diplomatic agents acting strictly within their official public functions.
Legislative acts enacted by a sovereign parliament regarding domestic natural resources.
Acta jure gestionis (commercial or private law transactions).

questions.question: Under Article 32 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (1969), when may recourse be had to supplementary means of interpretation, such as the preparatory work of the treaty (travaux préparatoires)?
options: In all cases, alongside the general rule of interpretation under Article 31, as a mandatory primary step equal in weight to the text.

Only to confirm the meaning resulting from the application of Article 31, or when interpretation under Article 31 leaves the meaning ambiguous or obscure, or leads to a result manifestly absurd or unreasonable.
Exclusively when all signatory parties explicitly agree in writing to consult the preparatory work during dispute settlement proceedings.
Only when interpreting multilateral human rights treaties, but never in disputes concerning bilateral economic agreements.

questions.question: In the landmark LaGrand case (Germany v. United States, 2001), what crucial determination did the International Court of Justice (ICJ) make regarding provisional measures indicated under Article 41 of its Statute?
options: Provisional measures are merely non-binding political recommendations that States should endeavor in good faith to follow.
Provisional measures automatically expire after 90 days unless confirmed by a formal vote of the UN Security Council.
Provisional measures indicated under Article 41 have binding legal force and create a legal obligation for the target State.
Provisional measures apply only to advisory proceedings and cannot be issued in contentious cases between sovereign States.
